messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty -> HIGH: stream-disconnect-rate spike for /v1/stream (p99 disconnects up 18% in last 3m)

Maya: paging oncall. I'm looking at the dashboard now, p50 latency ok but disconnects spiking. marking impact: some customers see sse disconnect + tool-call parse failures.

Omar: copying logs from edge for the last 10m. sending curl snippet I used to repro.

Omar: ```curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \n  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \n  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=toolcall-x' \n```

Omar: raw client-side snippet shows SSE connection established then `event: disconnect` after ~45s for some clients.

Kevin: I see a pattern: connections originating from us-east-1 ELB with older keepalive settings. Also seeing a flood of malformed tool-call payloads: `{"tool_response":"{...}\",\"meta\":...}` — looks like double-encoded JSON from some SDK versions.

Priya: customers on SDK v0.9.2 reported errors. new SDK v1.0 changed header framing for tool-calls, maybe backwards compat issue.

Maya: immediate mitigations: 1) throttle new streaming connections from the problematic pool to reduce storm, 2) enable fallback routing to non-streaming short-poll for flagged customers, 3) ask infra to roll keepalive patch to ELB. Omar, can you push the throttle?

Omar: on it. Applying k8s network policy to limit new SYNs to 30/s for the pool. Patch applied at 1891122387.

eng-runtime-bot: Deploy started: keepalive-fix -> edge-proxy (sha abc123). CI green. ETA ~6m.

Kevin: posted a sample parse failure in the thread: ```ERROR ParseToolCall: unexpected escape at pos 124 in payload "{\\\"tool_response\\\":\\\"{...}\\\"}"\nstack: parse.go:87```

Priya: hypothesis list — adding inline: 1) client SDK v0.9.2 double-encodes tool responses -> server parser throws -> connection error path triggers stream shutdown on server, 2) ELBs with old TCP keepalive drop idle connections while the client thinks stream is alive -> client retries and triggers parser edge cases, 3) recent runtime change to stream-framing made parser stricter, surfacing previously tolerated malformed payloads.

Maya: good. Assigning hypotheses: Priya -> #1, Kevin -> #3, Omar -> #2. We need timeline lines from 1891122000 -> now. Kevin, can you extract runtime logs for the timeframe?

Kevin: done. Pasting the condensed timeline: 
- 1891122045 edge-proxy saw spike in incomplete frames
- 1891122100 first parse errors in parser service (count 12)
- 1891122198 parser error rate climbs to 2.4%
- 1891122270 multiple clients reconnected quickly -> connection surge
- 1891122334 incident-bot page fired (root)
- 1891122387 throttle policy applied by Omar
- 1891122402 fallback routing enabled for customers flagged by support
- 1891122465 keepalive-fix deploy finished (edge-proxy)

Priya: I pulled customer-facing logs for acct:acme-inc. They show repeated `400 ParseToolCall` then a client retry which occasionally arrives mid-stream causing stream parser to get confused. Customer impact: 8 requests failed in their busiest window (~3% of their requests), degraded UX but no data loss reported.

support-ops: Support note drafted to inform impacted customers: short explanation, workaround to upgrade SDK to v1.0 or enable short-poll. Sending to legal for signoff.

Maya: live mitigation status: throttle in place, short-poll fallback enabled for flagged tenants, keepalive fix deployed. Current disconnect rate down from 18% -> 6% in 10m. Still above baseline. Next steps: 1) patch parser to accept double-encoded payload gracefully (hotfix) OR 2) release SDK patch that stops double-encoding. Which is faster?

Kevin: hotfix on server side is quicker — small change in parser to detect escaped outer string and unmarshal twice. I can put a canary behind feature flag for parser-safe-mode.

Priya: SDK patch will take longer due to release and churn across customers. Recommend server hotfix + coordinated SDK fix.

Omar: I'm going to keep the throttle for 30m then gradually remove once metrics stable. Will also add a client-compat header to responses to help us segment affected clients.

Maya: assigning tasks: Kevin -> parser hotfix canary; Priya -> prepare customer list + comms; Omar -> maintain throttle + telemetry header; Support -> send interim KB. I'll take point on post-incident RCA.

eng-runtime-bot: Canary deploy: parser-safe-mode -> parser-service (canary 5%) at 1891122590. Health checks passing.

Kevin: Canary logs show parse error rate dropped to near-zero for canary traffic. Rolling to 50% now.

Maya: after canary roll, disconnect rate back to baseline (1.1%). Great. We should keep parser-safe-mode for next 24h and make a proper patch + test matrix.

Priya: drafting postmortem outline in #incidents/rca: cause summary, timeline, mitigation steps, customer impact, followups (SDK bump, parser hardening, ELB keepalive defaults).

Maya: handoff to morning oncall (Omar) at 1891122800. Omar will monitor until 1891126400 and update the thread if anything flares. Thanks team. :tada:

Omar: ack, monitoring. I'll post telemetry every 30m.

support-ops: KB posted: "Intermittent SSE disconnects and tool-call parse errors — workaround and upgrade path". Link: https://support.redwood.ai/kb/sse-toolcall-compat

Maya: closing active mitigation. Leaving thread open for RCA notes and final writeup.

incident-bot: Incident update -> status: mitigated. Ticket: INC-2026-4421.
